AddDomainBody.description: Body for POST /api/domains. `projectId` is optional for API-key auth (derived from key) and required for session auth. `region` pins the SES region; on the first domain it locks the project, after that it must match the project's region. `stream` assigns the identity to transactional or marketing traffic at creation; omit it to leave the identity serving both.

region.description: Override SES region for this domain. Defaults to the project region or the env default. Required to match an existing project region.

streamDefault.description: Make this the project's default identity for `stream`. Requires `stream`. Setting it demotes whichever identity held it.

AddSuppression.description: Body for POST /api/suppression — manually add an email to the suppression list.

AnalyticsCampaignStatsV1.description: Campaign counters and engagement over the window.

AnalyticsTimeseriesV1.description: Daily email counters across the window. Every day in range is present, zero-filled.

AnalyticsTopCampaignsV1.description: Sent campaigns ranked by open rate.

AnalyticsWindowV1.description: The time range this response was computed over, after the 90-day clamp.

ApiKey.description: An API key's metadata. Never carries the token or its hash — `lastFour` is the only surviving fragment of the secret once the key has been created.

lastFour.description: Last 4 characters of the token — the only fragment of the secret that survives creation.

legacyGrantPreset.description: The coarse preset the key was minted under. It picks the token prefix (`sk_` vs `pk_`) and the rate-limit window, and it is the key's authority ONLY while `scopes` is empty — which is true just of keys minted before scopes existed. Read `scopes` to learn what a key can do.

mode.description: Where mail sent with this key may go. `LIVE` sends from your verified domains. `TEST` can only send from this project's sandbox address, whose recipient list is your own verified account addresses, so a test key cannot reach a customer whatever it is asked to do. Fixed at creation.

revokedAt.description: Set once the key is revoked. Revoked keys are NOT filtered out of list/get responses.

scopes.description: The explicit scope grant this key carries. Empty on a key minted before this column existed — that row's grant is derived from `legacyGrantPreset` instead at request time.

ApiKeyListResponse.description: Every API key on the project, including revoked ones — filter on `revokedAt` for live keys.

AppPassword.description: An IMAP/SMTP credential for one mailbox, described but never reproduced.

lastFour.description: The last four characters of the secret — enough to tell two credentials apart, and nothing more.

lastUsedAt.description: Null until a mail client has authenticated with it at least once.

name.description: What the credential is for, e.g. `Thunderbird on my laptop`.

scopes.description: Which protocols this password may authenticate. `imap` reads, `smtp` sends.

AppPasswordReveal.description: A newly created app password, handed over as a one-time link rather than as a secret.

revealExpiresAt.description: When the link stops working. Five minutes after creation; the password itself does not expire.

revealUrl.description: A single-use link that shows the password once, in a browser. Opening it requires a signed-in Sendly session belonging to a project admin — the connection that created the password cannot open it, and the second attempt to open it fails whoever makes it.

defaultFromAddress.description: The address a send on this stream uses when it names none. Must be on this identity's own host — a default pointing elsewhere would go out unsigned by the name in the From header.

defaultFromName.description: The name recipients see beside any address on this identity when a send names none, e.g. `Acme`. Independent of `stream`. An empty string or `null` clears it, and the project name is used instead.

stream.description: Which traffic this identity carries. `null` unassigns it, returning it to serving every stream and clearing its default flag and default address.

streamDefault.description: Make this the project's default identity for its stream, demoting whichever held it.

BatchEntryResult.description: Per-row result in a batch send response.

BatchSendBody.description: Batch send wrapper. Up to 100 entries.

BatchSendResponse.description: Multi-status response for `POST /api/emails/batch`. HTTP 207 if any entry failed, else 200.

from.description: Sender address. Its domain must be verified for this project.

list_id.description: Required when `audience_type` is `LIST`. Only that list's CONFIRMED members receive the campaign.

topic_id.description: The subject this campaign is about. A contact who unsubscribed from the topic is excluded WHATEVER the audience type — a topic opt-out is a standing answer, not an audience filter, so it cannot be routed around by selecting a different audience. CampaignV1Failure.description: A campaign recipient whose send did not complete.

email.description: The recipient the send was for.

id.description: Ledger row id. Pass the last one as `after` to page.

CampaignV1FailureList.description: Cursor-paginated list of a campaign's failed sends.

next_cursor.description: Pass as `after` to fetch the next page. `null` on the last page.

total.description: Every FAILED row on this campaign, not just this page.

next_cursor.description: Pass as `after` to fetch the next page. `null` on the last page.

CampaignV1RetryFailed.description: Acknowledgement that a retry of a campaign's failed sends began.

queued.description: How many FAILED rows the retry walk was started for, counted when it was queued.

scheduled_for.description: RFC 3339 timestamp, strictly in the future. A numeric UTC offset (`+02:00`) is accepted as well as `Z`. Omit to start sending immediately.

CampaignV1Stats.description: Materialized delivery and engagement counters for one campaign.

CampaignV1Update.description: Body for PATCH /api/v1/campaigns/{id}. All fields optional.

from.description: Sender address. Its domain must be verified for this project.

list_id.description: Required when `audience_type` is `LIST`. Only that list's CONFIRMED members receive the campaign.

topic_id.description: The subject this campaign is about. A contact who unsubscribed from the topic is excluded WHATEVER the audience type — a topic opt-out is a standing answer, not an audience filter, so it cannot be routed around by selecting a different audience. CompatMailgunError.description: Mailgun's error body: a bare `{ message }`. mailgun.js surfaces the status as `error.status`.

CompatMailgunMessageRequest.description: A Mailgun `messages.create()` form. Custom headers travel as `h:<Header-Name>` fields (for example `h:X-Campaign: spring`); `h:Reply-To` sets the reply address instead of becoming a custom header. Any other `h:` field is passed through as a header; other `o:` and `v:` options are ignored.

attachment.description: Repeatable file parts. Read and base64-encoded; a part with no content type is sent as `application/octet-stream`.

bcc.description: Repeat the field once per recipient.

cc.description: Repeat the field once per recipient.

from.description: A bare address or `"Display Name <address@domain>"`. Its domain MUST equal the `{domain}` path segment (compared case-insensitively), else `400`.

html.description: Preferred over `text` when both are sent.

o:tag.description: Repeatable. Each becomes a tag, stripped to `[a-zA-Z0-9_-]` and cut to 64 characters; at most 10.

subject.description: Required in practice: Sendly has no template mapping here, so a message without a subject is refused with `400`.

to.description: Repeat the field once per recipient.

id.description: `<{email id}@{domain}>`, with the first recipient's queued email id.

CompatPlunkError.description: Plunk's error body, the NestJS default exception shape.

CompatPlunkSendResult.description: Plunk's `{ success, emails, timestamp }`: one `emails` entry per recipient (a single request with an array `to` fans out), plus the send `timestamp`.

timestamp.description: ISO 8601 datetime string

CompatPostmarkBatchResult.description: One entry per input message, in order: a send result, or — for an entry that failed on its own — a `{ ErrorCode, Message }` object, with the request still answering `200` and the other entries still sent.

CompatPostmarkEmailRequest.description: A Postmark `/email` body. `From` and `To` are required, and so is one of `HtmlBody` or `TextBody` (else `422`).

HtmlBody.description: Preferred over `TextBody` when both are sent.

Subject.description: Required in practice: Sendly has no template mapping here, so a message without a subject is refused with `422`.

Tag.description: Becomes a single tag, stripped to `[a-zA-Z0-9_-]` and cut to 64 characters.

To.description: One or more recipients, COMMA-SEPARATED in a single string (Postmark's own convention).

CompatPostmarkError.description: Postmark's error body. The HTTP status is carried separately; the postmark SDK keys its thrown error class off it.

ErrorCode.description: Postmark's own vocabulary for the statuses Sendly emits: `10` (401, 403), `300` (400, 422), `701` (404), `429` (429), `100` (500); any other status is repeated here. The one exception is a body that is not JSON or whose root is not an object: it answers `402` with HTTP `422`, as Postmark does.

MessageID.description: The id of the queued email for the first recipient.

To.description: The request's `To` string echoed back, or `""` if it was not a string.

data.description: One `{ id }` per input entry, in input order.

html.description: The stored message body, whether it was sent as HTML or text.

last_event.description: Best-effort. `sent` when the row's delivery status is `SENT`, `failed` when it is `FAILED`, and `queued` for EVERY other status — including `DELIVERED` and `BOUNCED`. Read `GET /api/emails/{id}` for the real delivery status.

text.description: Always `null`; the body is returned in `html`.

to.description: Always exactly one address: the recipient of this row.

CompatResendEmailRequest.description: A Resend `emails.send()` body. Either `html` or `text` is required (else `422`). Translated to the native send input and then validated by the same schema as `POST /api/emails`, so its limits apply.

path.description: A URL to fetch the file from. NOT supported: Sendly never fetches a URL on a sender's behalf, so a request carrying `path` is refused with `422`. Send the file inline as base64 `content`.

from.description: Sender: a bare address or `"Display Name <address@domain>"`. The domain must be verified.

html.description: HTML body. Preferred over `text` when both are sent.

reply_to.description: Only the FIRST address is used; Sendly carries a single reply address.

scheduled_at.description: NOT supported. Any value other than `null` is refused with `422` (`COMPAT_UNSUPPORTED`).

subject.description: Required in practice: Sendly has no template mapping here, so a message without a subject is refused with `422`.

tags.description: Each tag becomes the single string `<name>_<value>`, stripped to `[a-zA-Z0-9_-]` and cut to 64 characters. At most 10 are kept.

template.description: NOT supported: a Resend template id cannot map to a Sendly template. Refused with `422` (`COMPAT_UNSUPPORTED`).

text.description: Plain-text body. Used only when `html` is absent.

to.description: One address or an array of addresses.

CompatResendError.description: Resend's error body. The resend SDK returns it as `{ data: null, error }`.

id.description: The id of the queued email for the first recipient. Poll `GET /api/compat/resend/emails/{id}`.

CompatSendGridError.description: SendGrid's error body, `{ errors: [{ message, field, help }] }`.

field.description: Always `null`: Sendly does not track which field failed.

categories.description: Become tags, stripped to `[a-zA-Z0-9_-]` and cut to 64 characters. At most 10 are kept.

content.description: The body is the first non-empty `text/html` entry, else the first `text/plain`, else the first entry with a value. At least one entry with a value is required.

personalizations.description: Each entry becomes its own send, with its own recipients. The whole fan-out is validated, and content review runs over it, before any send runs, so an invalid entry or a content refusal rejects the request with nothing sent. The sends then run one after another: a later send that fails (an unverified domain, a sandbox restriction, a rate or billing limit) answers an error and leaves the earlier entries queued.

subject.description: Overrides the top-level `subject` for this entry. Every entry needs a subject from one of the two places, or the request is refused with `400`.

to.description: At least one address is required.

subject.description: Optional only if EVERY personalization carries its own `subject`; an entry with neither is refused with `400`. The schema cannot express that either-or, so it is shown as optional here.

template_id.description: NOT supported: a dynamic template cannot map to a Sendly template. Refused with `400`.

ComposeMailboxMessage.description: Body for POST /api/mailboxes/{id}/messages — a new outbound message from a hosted mailbox.

document.description: Brandable email rendered by React Email. Text is escaped; images/GIFs use public HTTPS URLs. Columns stack on phones. No HTML, scripts, or arbitrary CSS.

src.description: Public HTTPS image or animated GIF URL; no upload or server fetch is performed
Public HTTPS image or animated GIF URL; no upload or server fetch is performed

ContactBulkDeleteBody.description: Bulk delete contacts. Provide either `ids` or `emails` (max 1000 each).

nextCursor.description: Cursor for the next page, or null on the last page.

ContactTopicPreferencesV1.description: Everything this contact has said about what they want. `subscribed` on a topic already folds in `default_opt_in`, so a contact who has never answered still reads correctly.

subscribed.description: The global marketing opt-out, which OUTRANKS every topic. False means no marketing reaches this contact whatever the topics below say.

key.description: Stable, URL-safe, unique within the project. This is what a preference form and an API caller name the topic by, so it must survive a rename of `name` — which is the whole reason it exists beside one.

subscribed.description: The EFFECTIVE answer: what the send path concludes for this contact today.

ContactV1.description: A contact as exposed on the v1 API.

custom_fields.description: Arbitrary JSON value (string, number, boolean, null, array, or object).
Arbitrary JSON stored on the contact and available to templates as `{{ variables }}`.

ContactV1Deleted.description: Acknowledgement that a contact was deleted.

next_cursor.description: Pass as `after` to fetch the next page. `null` on the last page.

ContactV1Update.description: Body for PATCH /api/v1/contacts/{id}. `email` is deliberately absent: an address is the contact's identity on this API, and changing it in place would silently rewrite what every earlier send was addressed to. Create the new address instead.

custom_fields.description: Arbitrary JSON value (string, number, boolean, null, array, or object).

mode.description: `LIVE` (default) or `TEST`. A test key can only send from the project's sandbox address, which accepts only the project's own verified account addresses as recipients, so it cannot reach a customer. Its sends are real sends down the same pipeline and are marked `sentInTestMode`. Fixed at creation.

scopes.description: The explicit grant the new key will carry. Omitted ⇒ materialised from `legacyGrantPreset`. A `SENDING_ONLY` key may carry only `emails:send`.

customFields.description: Arbitrary JSON value (string, number, boolean, null, array, or object).

domainId.description: A VERIFIED domain belonging to this project.

localPart.description: The part before the `@`, e.g. `support`. Lowercased server-side.

projectId.description: Defaults to the project the credential resolves to. Naming a different one is refused.

quotaBytes.description: NOT IMPLEMENTED — sending any value answers 400.

CreateWebhook.description: Body for POST /api/webhooks — register a user webhook for one or more events.

DeliverabilityDiagnosisV1.description: A composed answer to why mail from one domain may not be arriving: its DNS identity, the project's recent delivery outcomes, one address's suppression state, and the findings drawn from them.

findings.description: What is wrong, worst first. An empty array means nothing here explains a delivery problem.

DeliverabilityFindingSeverityV1.description: `blocking`: mail from this domain cannot be delivered as configured. `degraded`: it delivers, but inbox placement or sender reputation is at risk. `info`: worth knowing, nothing to fix.

DeliverabilityFindingV1.description: One diagnosed problem, with its fix.

code.description: Stable identifier for this finding, e.g. `domain_not_verified`. Branch on this, not on `summary`.

summary.description: What is wrong, in one sentence.

DeliverabilityIdentityV1.description: The sending identity's DNS health, as last refreshed.

dkim_status.description: DKIM signing. This is the one that decides whether Sendly will send from the domain at all.

last_checked_at.description: When the DNS refresh job last looked. These statuses are a CACHE, not a live lookup.

mail_from_domain_status.description: Raw SES `CustomMailFromStatus` (`Pending`/`Success`/`Failed`/`TemporaryFailure`), or `NotConfigured`. `Failed` means SES silently fell back to `amazonses.com`, which is why the value is reported rather than folded into a boolean.

mx_status.description: Inbound receiving only. Null unless the domain has receiving enabled.

registered.description: Whether this project has a domain record at all. False makes every other field null.

spf_status.description: SPF alignment for the sending identity.

DeliverabilityRecentDeliveryV1.description: Delivery outcomes over the requested window.

bounce_rate.description: Bounced ÷ sent (0–1), or null when nothing was sent in the window.

scope.description: PROJECT-WIDE, not per-domain, and said so rather than implied. `Email` has no sending-domain column, so narrowing these counters to one domain would mean a scan over every row the project has ever sent. A project that sends from one domain — most of them — can read these as that domain's.

DeliverabilitySuppressionV1.description: Null unless the request named an `address`.

pass_count.description: Messages DMARC-ALIGNED (SPF or DKIM aligned and passing), from `policy_evaluated`. Not the raw auth results: a message can pass SPF for a domain that is not the one in its From header, which is the case DMARC exists to catch.

policy_domain.description: The domain of yours the report is about.

report_id.description: The receiver's own id for this report.

sources.description: Per-sending-source rows, as the receiver reported them.

DmarcReportV1List.description: Cursor-paginated DMARC aggregate reports, newest window first.

intake_configured.description: Whether this deployment has a DMARC report intake mailbox configured. When `false` no report can ever arrive, so an empty `data` means the feature is off rather than that your domains are clean — the two are otherwise indistinguishable.

next_cursor.description: Pass as `after` to fetch the next page. `null` on the last page.

Domain.description: A sending identity: one domain registered with SES, with its own DKIM keys, its own MAIL FROM and its own reputation.

defaultFromAddress.description: The address a send on this stream uses when it names none. Always on this identity's own host.

defaultFromName.description: The display name recipients see beside any address on this identity when a send names none, e.g. `Acme` in `Acme <receipts@mail.example.com>`. A send's own `name` and its template's from-name both win over it; `null` falls back to the project name.

dkimStatus.description: Result of the last DNS check for this record type.

dkimTokens.description: SES DKIM tokens to publish as CNAME records before the domain can verify.

dmarcStatus.description: Result of the last DNS check for this record type.

mailFromDomain.description: Custom MAIL FROM subdomain SES has on record (normally `sendly.<domain>`).

mailFromDomainStatus.description: SES custom MAIL FROM setup state. Only `Success` means SES is using it.

receivingEnabled.description: Whether inbound mail for this domain is routed to Sendly mailboxes.

spfStatus.description: Result of the last DNS check for this record type.

stream.description: Which traffic this identity carries. `null` means unassigned, and an unassigned identity carries every stream — the behaviour of every domain added before per-stream identities. A send whose stream does not match an ASSIGNED identity is refused.

streamDefault.description: Whether this is the project's default identity for its stream — the one a send picks when it names no from-address. At most one per (project, stream).

DomainListResponse.description: List of all domains for the auth'd project.

DomainLogoReadinessV1.description: How ready a sending domain is to show its logo as the inbox avatar, per step and per inbox. Backed by public DNS and the customer's own web hosts, so a reading is held for a minute.

checked_at.description: When the lookups ran. A reading is held for a minute, so this can be up to a minute old; a fix to DNS shows after that.

items.description: `dmarc_enforced`: DMARC at p=quarantine or p=reject, pct=100, on the sending host and on its registered domain. `bimi_record`: a `default._bimi` TXT record whose `l=` is an https URL. `logo_file`: the file at `l=` is SVG Tiny PS (the file Sendly serves is always checked as served). `mark_certificate`: the record's `a=` URL answers with a PEM certificate (VMC or CMC); only that is checked, not the certificate chain. `gmail_profile_photo` and `apple_branded_mail`: routes that need no BIMI record and are set up with the provider, so they are always `unknown` (or `not_applicable`) and never `met`.

evidence.description: What was read (a record name and its value, a URL and what it answered), to compare with what you published.

reason.description: Plain English. Null when `status` is `met`; otherwise what is wrong, or why it cannot be checked.

status.description: `met`: checked just now and satisfied. `missing`: checked just now and not satisfied; `reason` says what to change. `unknown`: could not be checked, either because a lookup failed (check again shortly) or because the step is self-attested with the mailbox provider and invisible to us; never a pass and never a failure. `not_applicable`: depends on a step that is not done yet, or is not needed given another.

unlocks.description: The inboxes this step matters for.

providers.description: One checklist per inbox, in the order the steps should be done.

requirement.description: `required`: the inbox shows no logo without it. `optional`: helps or is accepted, and its absence does not block. `alternative`: a different route to a picture in that inbox that does not use the BIMI record.

status.description: `ready`: every `required` item is `met`. `not_ready`: a required item is missing. `unknown`: none is missing but one could not be checked. Readiness is not a promise: providers decide whether to display a logo.

DomainLogoV1.description: The logo mailboxes show beside mail from a sending identity, published through BIMI.

bimi_record.description: The DNS record that makes a mailbox fetch `url`. Publish it once.

png_url.description: The same logo as a 1024x1024 PNG, for the places that take no SVG (a Google account's profile photo, Apple Branded Mail). Served under the same rules as `url`.

readiness.description: What public DNS says right now. A provider shows the logo only when DMARC is `enforced` (p=quarantine or p=reject at pct=100) and the record is `published`. `unknown` means the lookup failed, not that the record is absent. Providers decide whether to display a logo. Gmail additionally requires a VMC or CMC certificate, which this does not check. DNS readiness alone does not guarantee display.

serving.description: Whether `url` answers today. It answers only once the identity has verified.

source.description: `default` is a monogram of the domain's initial, served until a logo is uploaded and again after one is removed.

svg.description: The SVG Tiny PS file `url` serves.

updated_at.description: When the upload was stored; null for `default`.

url.description: Where the logo is served. Stable for the life of the identity, so the BIMI record is published once and a new upload needs no DNS change.

svg.description: The logo as SVG source text, square, at most 64 KB. It is rebuilt into SVG Tiny PS — the profile BIMI requires — before it is stored; a file that cannot be (text not converted to outlines, a raster image, a <style> sheet, a canvas that is not square, over 32 KB once cleaned) is refused with a message naming what to change.

default_from_name.description: The display name recipients see beside any address on this domain when a send names none. `null` falls back to the project name.

mail_from_domain_status.description: SES's CustomMailFromStatus for `mail_from_domain` — the subdomain that carries the bounce path, NOT the status of any From address.

allOf.description: Which traffic a sending identity carries. An identity with no stream serves both, which is how every domain added before per-stream identities behaves.

region.description: AWS SES region for the project. Once a domain is added the region is locked and cannot be changed.

allOf.description: Which traffic a sending identity carries. An identity with no stream serves both, which is how every domain added before per-stream identities behaves.

stream_default.description: Make this the project's default identity for `stream`. Requires `stream`.

mailFromDomainStatus.description: SES custom MAIL FROM setup state. Only `Success` means SES is using it.

status.description: Raw SES DKIM verification status, e.g. `Success` or `Pending`.

tokens.description: DKIM tokens SES still has to report. Absent once verification has resolved.

DraftMailboxMessage.description: Body for POST /api/mailboxes/{id}/drafts — ask for help writing, never for sending.

deliveredAt.description: Accepted by the recipient's server, or null.

error.description: Why the email did not go out, as a sentence for its sender. Set only when `status` is FAILED, CANCELLED, REJECTED, RENDERING_FAILURE or BOUNCED; null otherwise, including while a send is waiting on a retry.

failureKind.description: Stable class of `error`, for code that branches on it. `refused` means Sendly declined the send and `error` says why (a limit, a disabled project, a consent rule). Null when `error` is null.

sentAt.description: Handed to the provider, or null.

EmailDeliveryStatus.description: Delivery lifecycle of the message. Engagement is reported separately.

EmailDetailResponse.description: One email and its delivery history.

EmailEvent.description: One transition in a message's delivery history.

timestamp.description: ISO 8601 datetime string

EmailTestV1.description: Receipt for a sandbox test send.

from.description: This project's sandbox sender — resolved server-side, never from the body.

id.description: The Email row this send created.

sandbox.description: Always true. It is here so a model relaying this result cannot describe a test send as a real one: the message came from the shared sandbox domain and could only reach the project owner's own inbox.

status.description: Delivery status at the moment of the response — `PENDING` for a send still queued.

to.description: The recipient the message was queued for.

id.description: The Email row this send created. Quote it in support requests.

to.description: The recipient the message was queued for.

emails.description: The addresses to check, at most 50. Every distinct DOMAIN costs a DNS round trip, so this endpoint is bounded by latency rather than payload size — validate a whole list with `POST /api/v1/lists/{id}/validation-runs`, which is a background job.

EmailValidationBatchV1.description: One verdict per address, in the order they were given.

EmailValidationResultListV1.description: One page of a run's results. No total — a run over a large list holds millions of rows, and the run's own counters are the numbers worth reading.

items.description: One address's verdict, with the evidence behind it.

next_cursor.description: Pass as `after` to fetch the next page. `null` on the last page.

EmailValidationRunV1.description: One bulk validation run over a list.

failure_reason.description: Set only on `failed`. Prose for an operator; never parse it.

processed_count.description: Addresses checked so far. There is deliberately no total: a list changes size while a run walks it, so a denominator captured up front would be wrong by the time you read it.

EmailValidationV1.description: One address's verdict, with the evidence behind it.

is_disposable.description: A throwaway-inbox provider. The ONLY flag here that lowers the verdict.

is_personal.description: A free/consumer provider (Gmail, Outlook). List-quality information, not a problem.

is_role_address.description: The local part addresses a role (`support@`, `info@`), not a person. List-quality information: role mailboxes are deliverable and companies answer them.

reasons.description: Human-readable findings. Prose for a person to read — branch on `verdict`, never on these.

EmailValidationVerdictV1.description: `deliverable`: the domain resolves and accepts mail, with no badness signal. `undeliverable`: the domain does not exist or publishes no MX records. `risky`: deliverable, but a throwaway-inbox provider — mailing it costs sender reputation. `unknown`: DNS did not answer in time, so this address was NOT checked. events.description: Delivery transitions for this message, oldest first. NOT the custom events recorded with `POST /api/v1/events` — those are a separate resource.

Public keys (`pk_*`) are restricted to the email-send endpoints and the self-serve list subscribe/unsubscribe pair; every other endpoint — event tracking included — answers 403 for them. OAuth2.description:
OAuth 2.1 with PKCE, for AI agents and other delegated clients (this is what the MCP endpoint at `/api/mcp` uses, and how a third-party application sends on a user's behalf). Tokens are minted through the consent screen and carry ONLY the scopes the user ticked there, so an operation lists the single scope it requires and a token without it answers `403` with code `SCOPE_MISSING` — before any input is parsed. Unlike an API key, a delegated token reaches an operation only where the route itself declares a scope; every other route refuses it outright.

**Ask for the right audience.** Pass `resource=https://app.sendly.now/api` on the authorization AND the token request to receive a token for this REST API; `resource=https://app.sendly.now/api/mcp` is the MCP endpoint's identifier. A request carrying no `resource` receives an OPAQUE token, which every endpoint here rejects. Each identifier publishes RFC 9728 metadata at `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/api` and `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/api/mcp`.

**Name the project on every call.** An OAuth grant belongs to a USER, not to a project — the same person may belong to several — so a delegated token carries no tenant and the project is chosen per request with the `x-project-id` header, checked against real membership. Omit it and a project-scoped operation answers `400`; send one the user does not belong to and it answers `403 PROJECT_ACCESS_DENIED`. List the projects a token may name with `GET /api/users/me/projects` (scope `projects:read`), which needs no header. API keys are unaffected: a key already names its project.
